text:
Kyle MacLean, an undrafted center from Verona, New Jersey, worked his way up through three seasons with AHL Bridgeport, and he came into this season with 172 NHL games, all for the Islanders. Through seven games he's playing about 10 minutes a night, with no points, two shots on goal and 20 hits. That last number is the job description.

The worry is what happens with him on the ice at five on five. The Islanders have taken just 37% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count) in his minutes, almost 14 points worse than the team does without him. If anything, the scoreboard has been kind to him.

One habit worth watching, from Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season: 36% of his setups came from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. He's a grinder with a passer's streak. Our numbers expect some points to come, around 12 over the rest of the season, but his value will be measured in shifts that end in the other team's zone, and so far there haven't been enough of them.
headline: Kyle MacLean's job is hits, not highlights
